programs.title_tr: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Toz Metal Kusuru & Yere İndirmeler
programs.title_en: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Powder Metal Defect & Groundings
programs.current_status_tr: Yüksek basınçlı türbin disklerindeki mikroskobik toz metal kirliliği nedeniyle küresel çapta yüzlerce A320neo/A321neo uçağı planlanmamış motor bakımına alındı. Ortalama motor revizyon süresi (TAT) 250-300 günü buluyor.
programs.current_status_en: Contaminated powder metal in high-pressure turbine disks required accelerated inspections; hundreds of A320neo family jets grounded globally with MRO shop turnaround times reaching 250-300 days.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY filosundaki yaklaşık 30-40 adet A320/A321neo uçağı yerde bekliyor; kapasite açığını kapatmak için ıslak kiralama (wet lease) ve mevcut A320ceo uçaklarının hizmet ömrünü uzatma yoluna gidildi. Pegasus filosu ağırlıklı CFM LEAP motorlu olduğu için doğrudan etkilenmedi.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Turkish Airlines has 30-40 A321neo aircraft parked; capacity shortfall managed via wet leases and extending older A320ceo service lives. Pegasus remains largely unaffected due to CFM LEAP engine selection.
programs.timeline_horizon: 2026 yılı boyunca ve 2027 ilk yarısına kadar sürmesi bekleniyor.
programs.source_reference: RTX Corporation / FAA Airworthiness Directives (AD 2024-0044) / THY KAP Açıklamaları

programs.title_tr: Boeing 737 MAX Üretim Kısıtı (FAA Aylık 38 Tavanı) & Tedarik Zinciri
programs.title_en: Boeing 737 MAX FAA Monthly 38 Cap & Supply Chain Bottlecks
programs.current_status_tr: FAA'in kalite ve montaj denetimleri kapsamında Boeing 737 üretimini aylık 38 uçak tavanında tutması ve Spirit AeroSystems gövde teslimat gecikmeleri nedeniyle 2026 teslimat takvimleri 3-6 ay geriye ötelendi. MAX 7 ve MAX 10 sertifikasyonu gecikmeye devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: FAA capped 737 production at 38/month pending quality audit milestones; Spirit AeroSystems fuselage supply constraints pushed airline delivery slots back by 3 to 6 months. MAX 7 and MAX 10 certification remains pending.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: SunExpress ve THY teslimatları planlanan takvimin gerisinde seyrediyor; havayolları yoğun yaz ve sonbahar kapasite planlamalarını mevcut gövdelerle optimize ediyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: SunExpress and Turkish Airlines delivery streams experiencing slot postponements; carriers optimizing utilization on existing fleet assets.
programs.timeline_horizon: Aylık 38 üretim tavanının 2026 sonuna kadar aşamalı olarak artırılması hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: FAA Oversight Directives / Boeing Quarterly Deliveries / Airline Fleet Filings

programs.title_tr: Airbus A321XLR Ticari Teslimatları & Dar Gövde Uzun Menzil Devrimi
programs.title_en: Airbus A321XLR Entry into Service & Long-Range Narrowbody Wave
programs.current_status_tr: EASA tip sertifikasyonunu tamamlayan A321XLR, Iberia tarafından Madrid-Boston hattında ilk ticari uçuşlarına başladı. 4.700 deniz mili (8.700 km) menziliyle dar gövdede transatlantik ve kıtalararası uçuş maliyetlerini %30 düşürüyor.
programs.current_status_en: Having achieved EASA certification, the A321XLR commenced transatlantic operations with launch customer Iberia. Its 4,700 nm range unlocks thin long-haul routes at 30% lower trip cost.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Orta Doğu, Afrika ve ikincil Avrupa şehirlerine doğrudan bağlantı potansiyeli nedeniyle bölge taşıyıcıları tarafından yakından izleniyor. THY ve Pegasus filo stratejilerinde uzun vadeli alternatif.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Closely monitored by regional carriers for secondary point-to-point routes into Africa, Central Asia and Europe; potential long-term fit for Istanbul network.
programs.source_reference: EASA Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS) / Airbus Commercial Aircraft Updates

programs.title_tr: Boeing 777-9 (777X) Test Uçuşları & Hizmete Giriş Tarihi
programs.current_status_tr: İtiş kolu bağlantı elemanındaki (thrust link) teknik arıza sonrası test uçuşları geçici olarak durdurulmuştu; Boeing ilk teslimat takvimini 2026 yılına (ve potansiyel olarak 2027'ye) revize etti. Başta Emirates ve Lufthansa olmak üzere amiral gemisi filoları A380 ve 777-300ER ömür uzatmak zorunda kaldı.
programs.current_status_en: Structural component inspection on engine thrust links required test fleet pause; initial deliveries rescheduled to 2026/2027. Major customers Emirates and Lufthansa forced to extend legacy 777-300ER and A380 service lives.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY'nin geniş gövde siparişlerinde Airbus A350-1000'e ağırlık vermesinde 777X gecikmeleri belirleyici stratejik etken oldu.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Delays were a primary catalyst for Turkish Airlines' decision to anchor its high-capacity widebody order book on the Airbus A350-1000.
programs.timeline_horizon: FAA tip sertifikasyonu ve ilk ticari teslimat 2026 sonu / 2027 hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: Boeing Defense, Space & Security / Airline IR Filings / Emirates President Statements

programs.title_tr: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Yüksek Basınç Türbini Dayanıklılığı & MRO Bekleme Süreleri
programs.title_en: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Hot-Section Durability & Shop Visit Backlogs
programs.current_status_tr: Sıcak iklim, tozlu hava sahası ve yüksek iniş-kalkış döngüsü altında çalışan LEAP motorlarında türbin kanatçığı erozyonu nedeniyle planlanandan erken motor indirme yaşanıyor. Küresel MRO atölyelerinde yedek parça ve motor kıtlığı devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: Harsh environment operations (heat, sand, high cycle utilization) causing premature hot-section turbine blade wear; global MRO shops experiencing parts constraints and extended turn-around times.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Pegasus'un filosunun belkemiğini oluşturan A321neo uçaklarında CFM LEAP-1A motorları kullanılıyor. Pegasus, proaktif motor rotasyonu ve yedek motor rezervasyonu ile uçak yerde kalma süresini (AOG) asgaride tutuyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Pegasus relies heavily on CFM LEAP-1A on its A321neo fleet; carrier leverages proactive engine rotation and buffer lease pools to keep AOG rates minimal.
programs.timeline_horizon: CFM'in güncellenmiş dayanıklı parça (durability kit) teslimatları 2026 boyunca yaygınlaşıyor.
programs.source_reference: Safran / GE Aerospace Engine Technical Briefings / Aviation Week MRO Watch

stories.article_body: Hong Kong, 21 October 2026: Emirates is commemorating 35 years of serving Hong Kong, building on a remarkable journey that took flight in July 1991. What began with Emirates’ first landing in Hong Kong has evolved into a longstanding relationship with the city, connecting generations of travellers with Dubai and destinations around the world, with its Fly Better promise at the heart of every journey. The journey began with the arrival of flight EK068 at the former Kai Tak Airport, marking Emirates’ debut in Hong Kong and a new chapter in the city’s aviation story. Operated as a thrice-weekly Dubai-Hong Kong-Manila service, the route made Hong Kong Emirates’ 22 nd destination from Dubai and its fourth in the Far East. “For 35 years, Hong Kong has been an important part of Emirates’ history from our first arrival at Kai Tak Airport to the introduction of new aircraft, products and experiences for our passengers. This anniversary allows us to reflect on our shared journey and look ahead towards the future. We remain committed to connecting Hong Kong with the wider world and enhancing the experience at every stage of travel. The sky is the limit,” said Sultan Alriyami, Emirates’ Hong Kong Area Manager. Over the years, Emirates has become a preferred choice for Hong Kong travellers. The airline introduced its flagship A380 service to the city in October 2010, followed by a fourth daily Hong Kong-Dubai flight in October 2013. It opened the Emirates Hong Kong Travel Store in July 2024, its first in East Asia, creating a dedicated local presence for customers. The momentum continued in 2025 with the arrival of Emirates’ latest retrofitted Boeing 777 and A380 cabins, bringing an enhanced onboard experience to travellers departing from Hong Kong. Today, Emirates serves Hong Kong with three daily flights, including two direct services to Dubai and a third daily service via Bangkok. Through Dubai, passengers can connect onwards to more than 138 destinations worldwide, including popular destinations among Hong Kong travellers such as London, Paris and Milan. stories.headline: Emirates Skywards Relaunches 'Mile-A-Minute' Loyalty Promotion for Dubai Visitors
stories.lead: Emirates and flydubai are incentivizing travel to Dubai by offering loyalty members one Skywards Mile for every minute spent in the city.
stories.source_description: Dubai, UAE, 22 October 2026: Emirates Skywards , the award-winning loyalty programme of Emirates and flydubai, is bringing back its popular ‘Mile-A-Minute’ offer, rewarding members with one Skywards Mile for every minute spent in Dubai, up to 7,200 bonus Miles. As Dubai welcomes its winter season of festivals, events and outdoor experiences, the limited-time offer adds an extra reward for international visitors enjoying a holiday or stopover in the city. First introduced in 2021, the popular initiative returns with an opportunity for members to earn bonus Miles on top of those earned on eligible Emirates and flydubai flight tickets. From discovering Dubai's cultural landmarks and world-class attractions to enjoying its diverse dining, shopping and entertainment experiences, members can make the most of their time in the city while getting closer to their next Skywards reward. Make every minute in Dubai count Emirates Skywards members who register and book an eligible return flight with Emirates or flydubai between 21 October and 5 November 2026, for travel between 21 October and 13 December 2026, can earn one bonus Skywards Mile for every minute spent in Dubai. Whether enjoying a short city break, a family holiday or an extended stopover, members can earn up to 7,200 bonus Skywards Miles, equivalent to five days spent in Dubai. The offer is available across all cabin classes and fare types on Emirates and flydubai. Earn even more Miles Beyond the Mile-A-Minute offer, Emirates Skywards members can continue to earn Miles through the programme's extensive network of hotel, retail and lifestyle partners across Dubai. Travellers staying at Atlantis The Palm can earn Skywards Miles on eligible hotel stays, while those looking to discover the city's desert landscapes and cultural attractions can earn or spend Miles on selected desert safaris and sightseeing tours with Arabian Adventures . Shopping enthusiasts can also collect Miles on eligible purchases at Dubai Mall , home to an extensive selection of international brands, dining destinations and entertainment experiences. For everyday purchases, members can download the Skywards Everyday app, save up to five payment cards and earn Miles at hundreds of participating brands across the UAE, spanning dining, shopping, wellness, leisure and more. With multiple opportunities to earn Miles throughout their visit, members can enjoy additional rewards beyond the bonus Miles earned through the Mile-A-Minute campaign. Turn Miles into memorable experiences Skywards Miles can be redeemed for flight tickets and upgrades on Emirates and flydubai, hotel stays and exclusive experiences through Skywards Exclusives . Members can also use Cash + Miles to reduce the cost of their next flight or on the Skywards Rail network in Europe. From their next getaway to an unforgettable live event, every Mile earned brings members closer to a world of rewards. To participate, members must: Register for the offer through emirates.com, the Emirates App, flydubai.com or other eligible registration channels by 5 November 2026. Book an eligible return flight originating outside the UAE between 21 October and 5 November 2026. Travel to Dubai between 21 October and 13 December 2026, with a minimum stay of 24 hours and a maximum stay of 30 days. Bonus Miles will be calculated based on scheduled arrival and departure times in Dubai and automatically credited to eligible members following their stay. The offer is available to Emirates Skywards members residing outside the UAE. Travellers who are not yet members can join the loyalty programme for free and register for the promotion before the booking deadline. For more information and to register for the offer, visit emirates.com . Terms and conditions apply.

stories.headline: Delta Air Lines Hosts 26th Annual DREAM Flight to Support Aviation Talent Pipeline
stories.lead: Delta Air Lines transported approximately 160 students from Atlanta on its 26th annual DREAM Flight to the Airbus U.S. Manufacturing Facility in Mobile, Ala.
stories.source_description: For approximately 160 aspiring aviators from across the Atlanta metro, Oct. 20 was the day the sky stopped being the limit. Students boarded Delta’s 26th annual DREAM Flight at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport for the Airbus U.S. Manufacturing Facility in Mobile, Ala., for a firsthand look at the careers that could one day be theirs. Students from local Atlanta schools and organizations including, Rex Mill Middle, Elite Scholars, the Kindezi Schools, Morrow High School, OBAP ACE Academy and The Atlanta Chapter of Tuskegee Airmen S.T.R.E.A.M. Program spent the day exploring what it takes to connect the world through flight and meeting the people who make it happen. Rotating through four interactive experiences, students toured the Airbus A320 Final Assembly Line and took part in a scavenger hunt on aircraft manufacturing. They tackled aviation-themed activities and challenges at the Old Canteen Center, operated drones and flight simulators at Flight Works and explored the Advanced Manufacturing Program and facilities at Bishop State Community College. Before heading home, students heard from a panel of Delta and Airbus leaders at Bishop State, including Kurt Ford, Managing Director of Flight Training; William Cossey, Managing Director of Supply Chain Management; Tyesha Gray, Director of Human Resources; Julian Anugom, Director of In-Flight Entertainment and Connectivity; and Roderick Rogers, Head of A220 Quality Product Improvement at Airbus. These leaders shared their own career journeys and answered questions about navigating the industry. “Every student on this flight has the potential to become a pilot, engineer, technician or leader. Representation can be a powerful catalyst for unlocking potential, especially when students see people who look like them building, flying and leading in this industry. Delta’s DREAM Flight helps them better understand the variety of career pathways in the aviation industry,” said Keyra Lynn Johnson, Chief Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Social Impact Officer. DREAM Flight’s founder honored This year, former Delta pilot and U.S. Air Force veteran John Bailey was inducted into the OBAP Hall of Fame at the organization’s annual conference. The honor recognizes Captain Bailey’s long career dedicated to opening doors for young people who dream of flying, from helping bring OBAP’s ACE Academy to Delta to founding Delta’s DREAM Flight. After flying military transport aircraft for the U.S. Air Force, including missions in Vietnam, Bailey joined Delta in 1973. As a newly hired pilot based in Boston, he often flew round-robin charter flights around the city for terminally ill children, and those flights sparked the idea to create a similar experience for kids who dreamed of becoming pilots. In July 2000, Bailey piloted the first DREAM Flight to the Smithsonian Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C., with 150 students from Atlanta City Schools on board. An all-Black crew of Delta pilots volunteered their time to operate the flight, and members of the Tuskegee Airmen greeted students in Washington. They returned to Atlanta on time, and 26 years later, DREAM Flight remains a one-day journey from takeoff to touchdown. Growing the next generation of aviators Delta’s DREAM Flight bridges the gap between early curiosity and future career options by building students’ interest in aviation through fun, hands-on educational experiences and pairing them with mentors. By making these foundational experiences readily available and financially accessible, Delta’s partnership with OBAP has successfully reached more than 4,000 young people to date. Many DREAM Flight alumni have gone on to build careers at Delta, including: First Officer Kyle Foley was just 12 years old when he boarded the very first DREAM Flight in 2000. Seeing the pilots and controls up close for the first time set him on a path that led to a career flying for Delta. First Officer Curtis Jackson took DREAM Flight as a teen and grew up looking up to Bailey as one of Delta’s pioneering pilots. Bailey’s advice to keep pushing himself until he reached his goals stayed with Jackson on his path to the flight deck. DREAM Flight is one of several Delta programs, including WING Flight , ACE Academy and the National Flight Academy , that introduce students to aviation careers and expand the aviation talent pipeline. Working together to expand horizons Airbus and Delta have long shared common goals for the future of travel from the talent in the industry to the aircraft to get us there. Earlier this year, Delta announced the addition of 31 next-generation Airbus widebody aircraft to its fleet, an investment that will fuel international growth and accelerate fleet renewal in the years to come. “We talk a lot about the future of aviation, but you can’t actually build that future without bringing new voices and fresh perspectives into the fold,” said Roderick Rogers, Head of A220 Quality Product Improvement in Mobile. “Opening our doors in Mobile to Delta’s DREAM flight is our way of showing these students that there is a very real, accessible place for them in this industry, whether that's in the cockpit or right here on the manufacturing floor.” Mobile is one of five cities worldwide where Airbus commercial aircraft are assembled. The Mobile Airbus U.S. Manufacturing Facility has more than 2,000 employees who produce A320 and A220 Family aircraft for customers in the U.S. and Latin America. Earlier this fall, Delta and Airbus also partnered on Delta’s 11th annual WING (Women Inspiring Next Generation) Flight, which brought 160 young women from Atlanta to the same Mobile facility in celebration of Girls in Aviation Day.
